question: Under the same paced native loop, does a latency-compensated schedule (plan each chunk at start+L_hat+1..+8, L_hat = max observed latency over the last 8 returns, public feedback only) keep planned slots executable where the naive schedule loses them, and what slack and failure remain?
pacing: identical to NA2: one tick per 16.667 ms wall; sense only with no ticket in flight and excluded from physical time

predictions.identity_check_not_finding: with an empty queue at return, STALE == min(8, max(0, elapsed - planned_offset))
predictions.naive: as NA2: d050 about 60% STALE, d150 100% STALE
predictions.compensated: first ticket behaves like naive (no history); afterwards STALE only when a latency exceeds the max of the previous 8 (expected rare, a few percent); slack = offset - elapsed mostly 0..2 ticks
predictions.cost_not_measured_here: the compensated chunk is predicted further ahead from an older observation; with the P0 engineering model its action quality cannot be judged

guard.on_violation: STOP: GUARD_TRIP.json records tick, q, qd, violations and held target; no further apply/start; pending DROPPED

target_admission: finite 9D target inside actual native joint limits, else REJECTED and the previous target is held; no clipping

policy.model: prior P0 engineering checkpoint (same bytes as NA1/NA2); actions known to be inaccurate
policy.worker: separate CPU process, CUDA hidden, fixed noise seed, 16-step DDIM, then declared return delay
policy.time_input: nominal offsets (offset+1..offset+8)*dt seconds, matching the planned slots

claims_allowed: STALE share and slack at return per schedule and delay
guard trips, if any, with the recorded violating joints and values
claims_excluded: that compensation preserves action accuracy (not measurable with P0)
